title: Move the waitlist into the private SaaS repo

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Follow-on to chatticus-3926bc (factor the marketing site out). Recorded now so
the boundary decision is on the record, not started until the Account model
this epic depends on exists — see the paid-enablement epic, chatticus-e26358,
as re-scoped by chatticus-16d3a9.

The waitlist is Anthus's sales funnel: prospect contact details, survey
answers, and scoring weights tuned to Anthus's professional-services business.
A self-hoster cloning Chatticus (the open product) has no use for it, and it is
the pre-account stage of the same lifecycle as Account. Under the
Organization/Account boundary this project settled on, it belongs in the
private repo (Chattic.us-web, or a later-split SaaS-specific repo if that
becomes warranted) alongside Stripe.

Carries: python/src/chatticus/waitlist/, waitlist_scoring.py,
waitlist_survey.py, waitlist_limits.py, http/waitlist_source.py, the operator
CLI, and the six waitlist_*.feature files plus their steps.

Not moving with this: chatticus-b2de88's decision that a dashboard is not
worth building before roughly two hundred signups, in favor of CSV export and
a weekly digest. That decision stands; this epic relocates the code, it does
not revisit the product call.

**Why not folded into the marketing split (chatticus-3926bc):** moving the
waitlist means relocating a live DynamoDB-backed store, five Python modules,
and an operator CLI, and it only makes sense once Account exists to attach
signups to. Splitting marketing first, with the waitlist API untouched and
still called same-origin from the new marketing host, keeps that project
scoped to routes, components, and static infra.

**Done when:** the waitlist store, scoring, and operator tooling run from the
private repo, and this repository (the open product) contains no waitlist
code, matching the "clones and deploys with no billing configured" guarantee
in chatticus-180e40.
